scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: Why does long-term stress make you forgetful — and make stress even harder to stop?
scenes.voiceover: Why does long-term stress make you forgetful — and somehow make stress even harder to stop?

scenes.visual: Cortisol drops rain on a mustard hippocampus blob; it visibly shrinks.
scenes.voiceover: Every stress burst floods your brain with cortisol. Short term: fine. But chronic stress keeps cortisol high — and it is toxic to your hippocampus, the part that handles memory.

scenes.visual: Triangle vicious cycle: STRESS → CORTISOL → HIPPO↓ → back to STRESS. Traveling dot loops endlessly.
scenes.voiceover: Here is the trap: your hippocampus is also your stress off-switch. Damage it — and your brain loses the ability to calm down. More stress, more cortisol, more damage.

scenes.visual: Teal BDNF spark zaps the small hippo; it springs back to full size; mustard ring blooms.
scenes.voiceover: The good news: exercise releases a molecule called BDNF — basically fertilizer for brain cells. Regular movement can actually reverse the damage and regrow the hippocampus.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; cortisol-shrink visual below. Norb curious.
scenes.cardText: Glucocorticoid toxicity: chronic cortisol physically shrinks the hippocampus, impairing memory and the brain's stress off-switch.
scenes.voiceover: Glucocorticoid toxicity: chronic cortisol physically shrinks the hippocampus — impairing memory, learning, and the brain's ability to turn stress off.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; BDNF grow-back visual below. Norb celebrating.
scenes.cardText:
20 minutes of walking, most days:
proven to trigger BDNF and restart hippocampal growth.
scenes.voiceover: Twenty minutes of walking most days. Studies show it is enough to trigger BDNF and restart hippocampal growth. The antidote is that simple.
